question.prompt:
A Pascal-like triangle has \(10\) as the top row and \(10\) followed by \(1\) as the second row. In each subsequent row the first number is \(10,\) the last number is \(1,\) and, as in the standard Pascal’s Triangle, each other number in the row is the sum of the two numbers directly above it. The first four rows are shown below.

[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_10B_Q03_question_fig1.svg)

What is the sum of the digits of the sum of the numbers in the \(11\)th row?

solutions.explanation:
We need the total of a row, so we can track totals without calculating every entry. Let \(S_n\) denote the sum of the numbers in row \(n\). The second row gives \(S_2=10+1=11\).

For any row \(n\ge2\), each interior entry contributes to two adjacent sums in the next row. The endpoints \(10\) and \(1\) each contribute to only one of those sums. Thus the interior entries of the next row total \(2S_n-10-1\). Adding its new endpoints gives
\[
S_{n+1}=(2S_n-10-1)+10+1=2S_n.
\]
Therefore, starting with row \(2\), the total doubles at every step:
\[
S_n=11\cdot2^{n-2}\qquad(n\ge2).
\]
There are \(11-2=9\) doublings from the second row to the eleventh row, so
\[
S_{11}=11\cdot2^9=11\cdot512=5632.
\]
The requested digit sum is \(5+6+3+2=\boxed{16}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Track the row totals
